bluf: iSocialWeb is a founder led Barcelona SEO and CRO boutique of 30 people, founded 2015, that sells traffic and conversion for hard cases, from hypergrowth targets to traffic recovery after migrations, and now leads its nav with AI SEO: a productised AI SEO Audit, a large llms.txt and an AI search log. The record shows awards (HuffPost's 2026 list of Spain's 50 best SEO agencies) and a claim of 300+ companies served, but not one named client. The Horus read is Neutral at 9.3, best placed for the click giving way to the citation. A rival should know the Monsoon read puts displacement at 65.3: this book buys on price.
doing:
The positioning line reads: Spanish digital marketing agency for traffic generation and conversion, specialised in complex situations from hypergrowth goals to post migration traffic recovery. In plain words: a search and conversion boutique that pitches itself for the difficult brief. The headline claim is rank plus volume: Spain's #1 SEO agency per The Huffington Post, trusted by 300+ companies.

The services page lists, in Spanish, SEO and AI SEO strategy, an AI SEO audit, link building, local SEO, Google Ads, Social Ads, CRO, A/B testing, analytics, interface design and content strategy. The lead lines at 3 are CRO (the meta description leads with improving conversion; CRO strategy and A/B testing pages) and SEO (the homepage banner claims #1 SEO agency in Spain; SEO heads six services). Core lines at 2 are AI Search / GEO (an AI SEO Audit page covering AI Overview, AI Mode and ChatGPT; a bilingual AI search log) and Data & Measurement (analytics implementation, data visualisation and GDPR privacy pages). Paid search and paid social score only 1. The one proprietary name is the AI SEO Audit. No partners and no CMS are listed.

The AI posture is visibility, not automation: it sells AI search visibility through the audit, GEO strategy, the large llms.txt and the news log, with original data such as a 39 project analysis of the sources AI cites; AI Automation / Agents scores 0.

Moves in date order: in 2021 it was ranked among Spain's top 5 SEO agencies by Marketing4eCommerce and took second prize for entrepreneurship from FEDE Agencias de España; in 2026 HuffPost listed it among Spain's 50 best SEO agencies. All are awards recorded in JSON-LD; no launch, hire, acquisition or client win is listed. The record lists no pricing model. Conspicuously absent for a shop claiming 300+ clients: any case study, named client, vertical or partner badge, and any Google or LinkedIn ad of its own.
clients:
The needs read counts 0 clients: no case study, no press release, no client slug and no testimonial survived into the record, so there is no observed need, no named only count, no mix and no shared client. The Radar files the client type as mixed and the home market as Spain, with the agency based in Cornellà de Llobregat outside Barcelona, and lists no verticals. The only client figure in the record is the homepage claim that more than 300 companies have trusted it, which the record can neither name nor test.

The silence is the finding. An SEO and CRO agency sells on before and after figures, and a record built from its own site holds none: no recovered traffic case, no hypergrowth case, no conversion lift, though the positioning line promises exactly those situations. The AI search log is the one place the record shows original work, and that work is market data (a 39 project analysis of the sources AI cites), not a client result. What the 300 companies came for is inferred from the sold mix, SEO and CRO first, AI search second, and the sentence says so.

What the base needs next: KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers scale faster than any channel before them) are its tailwinds, so it is likely, with moderate confidence, that its Spanish clients are sold the AI SEO Audit and GEO strategy on top of SEO retainers; KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out) is its headwind through SEO, so it is a roughly even chance that those retainers are repriced within the edition, and with displacement at 65.3 on the Monsoon read the repricing is likely to come from a cheaper rival rather than from the client.

openings:
The strongest opening is price: displacement is 65.3 on the Monsoon read, the mix is SEO and CRO hours, and 60% of the movable work would go to Latin America; a Spanish speaking rival delivering from there can undercut it line by line; likely, moderate confidence, the mixed client base moves on price. Second, the audit without the number: it sells an AI SEO Audit, but the read finds no audited AI visibility product (P1 partial), so a rival leading with citation share beats the audit; very likely, high confidence. Third, the CRO contradiction: a lead line at 3 with no testing tool on its own homepage, one slide for a rival whose house passes.

No public pricing (P5 unknown) leaves an outcome priced offer open.
